lanes.summary: REVIEWER CHECK answer: the author's claim is FALSE. `cta64_mma128_all_ones_at_256` builds only the "mma128" case via `cta64_sweep_cases(n).into_iter().find(|case| case.label == "mma128")`, times it, then calls `assert_all_ones_gemm(&c, n)` on a fresh C buffer. The CTA32 kernel (`gemm_cta_wmma_fp16`) is never launched there, so its output is not checked. The original test never checked CTA32 output either, so no assertion was lost. Judged against the round 2 scope: (a) the only assertion in the original test, `max_err < 1.0` at n=256 on the mma128 output, is still run by a non-ignored test. It is also still run inside the ignored sweep via `assert_all_ones_gemm`. The new standalone test is stricter than the original, because C starts at 0 and only mma128 writes to it. A PTX load failure now fails the test, where the sweep silently skipped the check. (b) The helper keeps the condition `max_err < 1.0`, the expected value `n as f32` (K, since the matrix is square), and the message `"64x128 correctness FAILED at {n}: max_err={max_err}, expected={expected}"` exactly. (c) The marker is `#[ignore = "FLAKE-0 #4593"]`. I also compared the per-kernel launch shapes (PTX entry, sm_80 target, grid, block, shared memory) against the original and they match. CTA32, CTA64 and Dbuf64 compile failures still skip the size row (`None if case.required => return`). The other kernels read ∞ on failure. Gaps: the roadmap acceptance criteria still say "no other test changes" and carry the superseded REVIEWER CHECK wording, which is cosmetic under the round 2 scope. GPU execution is not_measured, as the receipt says. The OOM fix is out of scope.
